property_summary: For any caller and any payable amount sent to go(), the reference contract always forwards any remaining balance to the contract owner (so address(c).balance == 0 after go()), whereas the mutant sometimes leaves funds at c or sends them to msg.sender causing address(c).balance != 0 or owner not receiving funds.

For every admissible call to go(amount, caller), contract C always ends with zero balance (it forwards all remaining Ether to owner); the mutant that transfers remaining balance to msg.sender can leave nonzero balance in C for some caller/amount when the external target call forwards funds back into C (via a malicious callee), violating address(c).balance == 0.

For any caller and any value, after calling go() where the external target may re-enter and send Ether back into C, the reference always ends with address(c).balance == 0 because it forwards remaining balance to owner, whereas the mutant that transfers to msg.sender can leave nonzero balance in C for some re-entering target.

For every caller and any sent ETH, after go() finishes the contract C forwards any leftover balance out of itself (so address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that transfers leftover to msg.sender can leave nonzero balance in C when the external target re-enters and sends ETH back into C, violating address(c).balance == 0 for some inputs.

For every call to go(msg.value) where the callee (target) may forcibly send ETH back into C, the reference contract always ends with address(c).balance == 0 because it forwards remaining balance to owner; the mutant that forwards remaining balance to msg.sender can leave a nonzero balance in C for some adversarial callee that sends ETH back, violating that property.
